topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The opening connects the lecture to the histopathology practicals and outlines what students should learn.

topics.label: Tumor virology and the discovery of cellular proto-oncogenes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how research into cancer-causing viruses revealed that transformation originates in altered cellular genes.

topics.label: Experimental tests of cellular transformation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how laboratory assays establish whether a gene or mutation produces transformed cellular behavior.

topics.label: Cancer gene function and the effects of mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations are classified by their effects on tumor formation and why those effects depend on the affected protein's function.

topics.label: Genetic instability and defective DNA repair
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish sequence from chromosomal instability and explain how failures in DNA repair produce these phenotypes.

topics.label: Genetic instability from replication and mitotic errors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how errors during genome copying and segregation generate instability that can promote tumor adaptation.

topics.label: Mutation order in colorectal cancer progression
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how the timing of mutation acquisition and genetic instability affects the progression from normal tissue to metastatic cancer.

topics.label: Inherited cancer predisposition and tumor suppressor defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics follow inherited tumor suppressor defects through cancer development, with BRCA2 restoration illustrating that the initiating defect need not remain necessary for malignancy.

topics.label: Further reading, questions, and next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: The closing returns to the learning outcomes and offers questions, recommended reading, and a preview of the next lecture.
